stemMd:
At point **[2]** in paragraph 3, the writer is considering adding the following sentence:

> The library also runs a monthly book club that meets in the same room as the seed cabinet.

Should the writer make this addition?

options.label: A
options.textMd: No, because the book club has already been described earlier in the passage.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Yes, because it tells the reader where the seed cabinet is kept.

options.label: C
options.textMd: No, because it introduces a detail that does nothing to develop the paragraph’s point about what the collection records.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Yes, because it shows that the library serves its community in more than one way.

explanationMd:
Work out what the paragraph is doing before you judge the sentence. Paragraph 3 makes one point: the borrowing record has become evidence of a changing climate. Every sentence in it supports that point — beans finishing earlier, okra becoming the most borrowed packet, the extension office citing the ledger.

A book club is a true and pleasant fact about the library, but it says nothing about what the collection records, so it interrupts the paragraph’s line of thought. The addition should be rejected.

Check your answer by reading the paragraph with the sentence inserted: if you cannot say what the new sentence adds to the paragraph’s argument, it does not belong. Note also that a choice can give a true reason and still be wrong — the question is not "is this interesting?" but "does this serve the paragraph?"

distractorRationale.d: Accepts the sentence because the information is agreeable and true. Relevance on the ACT is judged against the purpose of the specific paragraph, not against the passage’s general subject; showing the library is versatile is not what paragraph 3 is doing.
distractorRationale.b: Treats an incidental clause ("in the same room as the seed cabinet") as though location were the point. The paragraph is about what the ledger data show, and the reader has no need of the cabinet’s location at this point.
distractorRationale.a: Rejects the sentence for a reason that is factually false: the book club is never mentioned anywhere else in the passage. Always verify a claim about what the passage already says before choosing an answer that rests on it.

accessibilityText: The question asks whether to add the sentence "The library also runs a monthly book club that meets in the same room as the seed cabinet" to the third paragraph, which is about what the seed-borrowing records show about the local climate.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Paragraph 3's point is that "the collection has become a record of a changing climate"; a monthly book club is irrelevant to that record, so the sentence should be cut. D is factually false (no earlier book-club mention) and A/B offer true-sounding but off-topic justifications.
